terms.gloss: a vote; the right to vote
evidence: Cic. Fam. 11.27.7: ego tē suffrāgium tulisse in illā lēge prīmum nōn crēdidī
M-O s.v. vote vb.; vote: ballot
terms.comment: To vote is suffrāgium ferre (Cic., Varro; Traupman 181; M-O). Lewis & Short: a voting tablet, a vote, and the right of voting; Morgan–Owens adds jūs suffrāgiī for the right to vote. A Roman citizen voted in his century or tribe at the comitia (see election).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent, with the dative
terms.comment: Of voters and, by extension, of anyone who backs a person or a cause (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Leg. 3.39: habeat sānē populus tabellam quasi vindicem lībertātis
terms.comment: The tablet of the secret ballot, brought in by the four lēgēs tabellāriae (Cic. Leg. 3.35). A ballot box is urna, the Roman voting urn (Lewis & Short; M-O), or Traupman’s suffrāgiōrum cista (Traupman 178).

terms.gloss: a senator’s vote: the opinion he states when asked
evidence: Traupman 181: discessiō facta est in ejus sententiam, a vote was taken on his motion
terms.comment: Senators did not cast ballots: each gave his sententia when asked, and the house then divided by walking to one side (discessiō, below). Traupman gives cēnseō for a senator’s vote (Traupman 181).

terms.gloss: a division of the house: a vote taken by people moving to one side
evidence: Cic. Sest. 74: fieretque sine ūllā varietāte discessiō
Traupman 181: discessiōnem faciō, call for a vote
terms.comment: To put a motion to the vote this way is discessiōnem facere (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ego tē suffrāgium tulisse in illā lēge prīmum nōn crēdidī
phrases.english: to begin with, I didn’t believe you had voted on that law
on election day they all asked for ballots

phrases.latin: habeat sānē populus tabellam quasi vindicem lībertātis
phrases.english: by all means let the people have the secret ballot, as the guardian of its freedom
